headline: Sales and profit jump as Lifyorli launch adds fuel
summary_short: Corcept's Q2 2026 net product revenue rose 31.7% y/y to $256.1M as Hypercortisolism Products sales grew and newly-launched cancer drug Lifyorli contributed its first quarter of sales, while diluted EPS rose 24.1% to $0.36 and gross margin held near 98%.
summary_long: Net product revenue rose 31.7% y/y to $256.1M on Hypercortisolism Products growth (volume, an August 2025 price increase, and better payor reimbursement, partly offset by lower-priced generic mix) plus Lifyorli's first quarter of sales after its April 1, 2026 launch. Cost of sales fell to 1.6% of revenue on lower manufacturing costs; R&D fell 10.9% to $53.9M as programs matured; SG&A rose 51.0% to $156.9M on commercialization spend for both products. Operating income rose 54.8% to $41.3M and diluted EPS rose 24.1% to $0.36. No forward guidance was given. Cash, equivalents and securities ended at $544.6M (up from $532.4M); no stock was repurchased in H1 2026 versus $130.5M in H1 2025.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven by higher Hypercortisolism Products revenue (volume, an August 2025 price increase, and improved payor reimbursement, partly offset by higher lower-priced authorized-generic mix) plus Lifyorli's first quarter of sales after its April 1, 2026 launch.
Cost of sales fell to 1.6% of revenue from 1.8% on lower manufacturing costs for Hypercortisolism Products; Lifyorli's pre-approval drug cost was expensed as R&D, not cost of sales.
Same underlying driver as gross profit: lower manufacturing costs for Hypercortisolism Products, per the release.
Operating income rose as higher revenue and a 10.9% R&D decline outpaced a 51.0% rise in SG&A tied to commercialization of both Hypercortisolism Products and Lifyorli.
EBITDA tracks the operating-income improvement plus depreciation/amortization add-back; the filing does not discuss EBITDA as a distinct measure.

Net income growth reflects the operating income increase, partly offset by a swing from a $3.5M tax benefit to a $2.9M tax expense on lower stock-compensation tax deductions, plus slightly lower interest income.
Basic EPS grew slightly slower than net income as weighted-average basic shares rose to 105.4M from 104.1M.
Diluted EPS grew faster than net income as diluted weighted-average shares fell to 118.4M from 120.5M on fewer dilutive stock awards outstanding.

Growth this quarter layers Lifyorli's commercial launch (approved for platinum-resistant ovarian cancer) on top of continued Hypercortisolism Products gains, with no company guidance provided in this filing.
